Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office files ordinary paperwork by assigning each submission a unique identifier, logging the date and time of receipt, and storing the submitted forms, field values, and attached media in a sequential index for later review by authorized personnel.

2) What occurred: The actor opened a named account and recorded a dated ticket reference. The actor produced multiple digital ticket images derived from a single dated record. The actor recorded each copy's file metadata as a separate dated field. The actor transmitted several digital ticket images through a message channel to an unnamed recipient account. The actor recorded the message channel timestamp as a field. The actor omitted the source ticket verification signature from each copied document. The actor recorded a payment reference for multiple copies against a single dated ticket record.

3) Materials/access observed: One named account, one dated ticket record, several digital ticket images, one message channel, several recipient account identifiers, one payment reference, and several file metadata fields.

4) Indicators & artifacts: Multiple dated ticket images sharing a single source identifier; file metadata timestamps predating the original dated record; absence of a verification signature on each copied document; several recipient account identifiers linked to one payment reference; message channel timestamps preceding the original dated record.
